Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads-up and for the extract. I pulled our server-side metrics and confirm ~58,400 extra inference minutes for August (model: redwood-large-v2, average seq len ~420).

Options we typically offer: 
- One-time top-up invoice for the excess usage (net 30)
- Apply a goodwill credit (partial) if the spike aligns with a documented incident we caused (not the case here)
- Convert the excess into committed delta for the remainder of the term (would require an amendment)

If you want the quickest path, PO -> one-time invoice is fastest. I'll draft the invoice details and send over the PO line items. For transparency I'm attaching our usage breakdown so procurement can match line items to their PO.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Lead, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Mark — quick answers: the usage tally Kimber provided is deduplicated and excludes retries (we strip server-side retried attempts and only count completed tokens generated). Unit pricing used is the committed per-minute rate in FC-2025-EXP-09 plus overage rate for the delta.

I ran the numbers and the one-time invoice amount comes to $12,540 (before tax). I've attached a proposed invoice PDF and a PO template. If you can provide a PO number and confirm Net30 is acceptable, we'll submit through finance and signal to collections.

If you need Net45, we can accept that but it will trigger a 1.5% processing surcharge per Redwood's standard policy for extended terms (we can also absorb half of that if needed as a one-off to keep things moving).

Best,
